name: Tablada airfield (Army of Africa airlift), Seville
story: With the Republican navy blocking the Strait, Franco's Army of Africa was stuck in Morocco. From late July 1936 German Junkers Ju 52 and Italian Savoia-Marchetti transports flew legionnaires and Regulares from Tetuán to Seville — the first large military airlift in history, landing mainly at Tablada and at Jerez. The troops then marched north to Badajoz and Madrid. The airfield was a military base and aviation school afterwards.
see: A military base; only its perimeter can be seen.
